content: The purpose of screening for nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is to detect individuals who are at an increased risk of developing serious health complications associated with nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH). These complications include cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and liver-related mortality. The risk of these outcomes is particularly high in individuals who have central obesity, cardiometabolic risk factors, or insulin resistance. However, there are limitations to relying solely on insulin resistance and cardiometabolic factors as indicators for screening, as their predictive value may vary. For example, hypertension has a lower specificity when used as a marker for insulin resistance. Furthermore, some young adults and lean individuals may exhibit liver steatosis and insulin resistance even in the absence of traditional cardiometabolic risk factors.
